vignette: Jason, a 25-year-old African American journalist, experienced a traumatic event involving police violence during his work coverage. The incident, which occurred several months ago while he was reporting on a protest, left him with vivid and haunting memories that continue to impact his daily life. The night of the trauma, Jason witnessed an intense confrontation between protesters and law enforcement officers. He heard the unmistakable sounds of sirens, shouting, and the distant pop of tear gas canisters being deployed. Suddenly, amidst the chaos, he saw a young protester collapse after being hit by what appeared to be a rubber bullet fired by police. The scene was overwhelming — the smell of smoke, the sound of shattering glass, and the echoes of protesters' cries for help. Since that night, Jason has found himself hyper-sensitive to certain triggers. The sound of footsteps behind him sends a wave of anxiety through his body, reminding him of the sense of being pursued during the incident. Similarly, certain songs from that day trigger intense flashbacks, making it seem as though he is reliving those terrifying moments. These triggers have led Jason to adopt various maladaptive strategies to cope with his heightened state of alertness. He wears concealing clothing to avoid drawing attention to himself and tries to keep his distance from grief reminders, such as news reports or events that remind him of the protester who was injured. This avoidance behavior has also extended to a broader fear of experiencing any strong emotions, both positive and negative, which he believes could destabilize his fragile emotional equilibrium. Jason’s difficulty concentrating is a significant challenge in his work environment. He struggles to focus on stories that require him to be out in unfamiliar places, as the uncertainty heightens his sense of danger. He frequently looks behind him to check if someone is following him, a behavior that has become almost second nature. His concentration issues have made it difficult for him to complete assignments on time, leading to tension with his colleagues and a decline in his overall performance. The memories of the traumatic event feel more real than any other memory he possesses. He often finds himself vividly recalling the sounds from that day — the sirens, the shouting, even the popping sound of tear gas canisters. When he attempts to recount what happened to others, he loses track and cannot fully articulate his experience, leaving him feeling frustrated and misunderstood. Jason has come to believe that his life has been irrevocably altered by this trauma. He feels a deep sense of loss for the happier person he used to be and now views himself as someone who is no longer capable of doing the things that defined his identity before the incident. These negative appraisals have reinforced his maladaptive strategies, leading him to further isolate himself from situations that could trigger traumatic memories. The interplay between these factors has created a self-reinforcing cycle. His triggers — footsteps and certain songs — not only evoke vivid memories but also heighten his sense of threat, making it difficult for him to function normally in daily life. The memory of the event feels more real than any other, further exacerbating his negative appraisals about himself and his future. This heightened state of vigilance has led Jason to avoid unfamiliar places and people, which in turn reinforces his belief that he is no longer capable of performing as a journalist. Jason’s avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on his relationships and work performance. He finds it increasingly difficult to engage with colleagues and friends without feeling anxious or withdrawing into himself. His once vibrant life now feels constricted by the constant reminders of that fateful night. What finally brought Jason to seek help was a culmination of these factors — the escalating anxiety, the impact on his career, and a growing fear that he might lose touch with who he used to be entirely. He is hoping for relief from the overwhelming sense of threat and a chance to reclaim some semblance of the life he had before the trauma.
